evidence: Three top-level packages (function, utils, docs) suggest logical grouping of concerns rather than strict layers
No explicit layer boundaries (e.g., no 'presentation/', 'service/', 'domain/' directories); instead, 'function/' contains domain-specific scraping modules (search, detail, review)
Shared utilities in 'utils/' are used across domain modules without strict dependency directionality
Main entry point (main.py) orchestrates components directly without a clear separation of concerns into layers
Low average fan-out (1.25) indicates modules depend on few others, consistent with cohesive modules in a monolith
No inter-service communication patterns (e.g., no HTTP clients to external services beyond internal scraping targets), ruling out microservices-like
No ports/adapters separation (e.g., no clear boundary between core logic and I/O adapters)
No MVC structure (no templates/views, no controllers handling HTTP requests/responses in a standard way)
risks: Tight coupling between utility modules and domain functions may reduce testability
Lack of explicit layering may lead to ambiguous separation of concerns over time
Centralized controller (spider_controller.py) may become a bottleneck and single point of failure
